definitions.note: plural answer; 'in dire straits' means in difficulty

indicators.note: the points sit outside, so the feature word is enclosed by them

parts.note: two compass points, S and S (south twice)
a trait is a characteristic feature

explanation.surface: Someone highlights a feature that is giving trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' here means 'on the outside': S and S go outside TRAIT. 'causing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Straits, as in 'dire straits', is a predicament or trouble.

clue.text: Longed for a party, we hear

indicators.note: the hearers' report signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: Someone yearned for a celebration, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a party' looks like what was longed for; 'party' is SIDE, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sigh for something is to yearn or pine after it.

clue.text: Criticise notes one's written in a hurry

indicators.note: the notes and the one are put down inside the hurry word

parts.note: a rush is a hurry
B is a musical note; two of them for the plural
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone scrawls their notes hastily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a hurry' looks like how the notes were written; it is the container. 's (is) is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish something is to disparage or pan it.

clue.text: En route popular northern artist breaks down

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: breaking down suggests the letters fall apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: A well-liked artist from the North collapses on the way somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' rearranges N plus ARTIST into TRANSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in transit means travelling, on the way to a destination.

clue.text: Ship out wheel for road vehicle

indicators.note: the ship is placed on the outside, enclosing the wheel word

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship
to wheel or roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: A ship's wheel is brought out for a road vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' means on the outside here, not removed; 'wheel' is the verb, to turn over. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy machine with a large drum that flattens road surfaces.

parts.note: to will something is to leave it by bequest
g is the symbol for the force of gravity

explanation.surface: A will remains in force, according to a lawyer discussing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is the adjective: ready and eager, as in 'I'm game'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being game means being ready and eager to have a go.

indicators.note: taking time off means removing it from the word

parts.note: want means lack, as in 'for want of'

explanation.surface: Someone without leisure time looks unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wan face is pale and unhealthy-looking.

indicators.note: 'say' signals a word that is pronounced like another

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it out, so 'let' as a past form is leased

explanation.surface: A landlord rents out the smallest possible flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the smallest amount possible.

parts.note: in means at home
a place is a location

explanation.surface: Someone establishes a household at a chosen site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link joining the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in place is installed or arranged and ready.

clue.text: Cheer German girl holding object up

indicators.note: the girl word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A German girl cheers while holding something aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' is the noun meaning aim; 'up' reverses it because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheer here is joy or happiness.

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
between, as a road between two towns joins them

explanation.surface: An attempt to bring a stockbroker into a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary who negotiates for two parties.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A Greek appears in a surreal fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter run spans the end of 'surreal' and the start of 'phantasy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet.

indicators.note: the one cuts into the other piece, sitting inside it
turned around means the word is written backwards

parts.note: an acre is a unit of area
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts back around a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns ACRE into ERCA; I cuts into it. 's (is) is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the genus of heathers.

parts.note: not the internet: a service running on a railway line that carries letters

explanation.surface: An email provider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' tempts towards email, but the line is a railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: A train that carried post along the rail network.

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is in
otherwise means different, other than expected

explanation.surface: A cricket remark about a batting average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting average' reads as one cricket term, but 'average' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifferent means mediocre, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Shows Fred crate of reproduction furniture

indicators.note: a reproduction is a remade copy, so these letters are made again in a new order

explanation.surface: Fred displays a crate of reproduction furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduction' looks like it describes the furniture; it rearranges SHOWS FRED CRATE. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of bedroom furniture: a set of drawers in a frame.

parts.note: awe is reverential fear
struck means hit or attacked

explanation.surface: A victim is overcome by fear after being assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone awestruck is filled with wonder, overcome.

definitions.meaning: a college fellow is a university scholar

explanation.definitionFit: A question that is merely theoretical is academic; a scholar at a university is an academic.

parts.note: not one of the seven sins: a crime punished by death, 'deadly' read as fatal for the offender

explanation.surface: One of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deadly sin' calls up pride or envy; here it is a crime that once carried the death penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime punishable by execution, sin standing for crime.

indicators.note: the silver lines the inside of the other word

parts.note: passé means outdated, old hat
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An old hat with a silver lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver lining' suggests the proverb; AG lines PASSE. 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is an excerpt from a book or piece of music.

clue.text: First of clarinettists plays unusual love song

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken
unusual signals the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A clarinet player performs a strange love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love song' reads as one phrase, but 'love' gives the final letter and 'song' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean style of song.

clue.text: Optimistic pound will show initial increase

parts.note: an increase is a rise, a going up; 'initial' places it at the start
to pound is to beat

explanation.surface: A sterling rise brings cheer to the markets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' tempts as sterling; it is the verb meaning beat. 'will show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful and positive.

definitions.meaning: to release, as a prisoner from custody

explanation.definitionFit: To discharge cargo is to unload it; to discharge a patient or prisoner is to release them.

clue.text: Urgency, as required in the run?

indicators.note: the word as is placed inside the other piece
a run of letters can be scrambled, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Speed is needed when one is in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the run' suggests a race; 'run' scrambles the word before it to HTE. 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurry or speed in acting.

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: to tug is to pull
a lip is a rim or border

explanation.surface: Someone nearly drags up a flower from the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a flower border; it is LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip is a spring-flowering bulb.

clue.text: Agency base enhanced by a quarter

indicators.note: the base word is increased by having the quarter added to it

parts.note: mean means base or ignoble
S, south, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A firm's base is strengthened by a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A means is the agency or method by which something is done.

clue.text: Bishops put helper in a flap

indicators.note: being in a flap means flustered, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Bishops put their helper into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flap' rearranges PUT HELPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The purple is the rank of bishops and cardinals, from their purple robes.

clue.text: Either way it's a little one

indicators.note: read forwards or backwards the letters are the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A child, whichever way you look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child.

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so it goes inside

parts.note: cement is something that bonds
L is the abbreviation for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: The Pope's money is put into bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in bond' reads as finance; L goes inside CEMENT. 's (is) is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement is a name taken by several popes.

definitions.meaning: to escort someone on an outing

explanation.definitionFit: To take out a tooth is to remove it; to take someone out is to go on a date with them.
